title: LTX-2.5, node by node
hook: Eight model calls, a fixed noise list, video and sound in one latent: read the real graph one node at a time.

verified.claim: LTXVConditioning writes frame_rate into both conditionings, and the model divides time coordinates by it.
LTXVConcatAVLatent packs video and audio into one NestedTensor, and LTXVSeparateAVLatent unpacks them.
The graph's sigma list equals DISTILLED_SIGMA_VALUES in Lightricks' code, and that code's default is 121 frames at 24 fps.
The file names in the graph follow the file names in the LTX-2 README, with a quantized copy of the transformer and encoder.
The lab's LTXVScheduler port gave the same 8 sigmas as the real LTXVScheduler.execute at 4096 positions.
The graph passes validate_prompt with its file menus skipped. It was not run for this lesson.
The gallery clip has 145 frames at 960 x 544 and stereo sound at 48000 Hz.

unchecked: The LTX-2.5 weights are not on our test machine today, so we did not run this graph for this lesson. The clips come from earlier renders recorded in the gallery data.
The audio latent sum uses the default config in causal_audio_autoencoder.py. A checkpoint can carry its own config, and we did not open the LTX-2.5 audio VAE to read it.
We read in Lightricks' constants that a second-stage sigma list exists, and the README's distilled command takes a spatial upsampler. We did not compare one stage against two.
